text:
A low-carbohydrate intake can reduce glycogen stores and lead to fatigue, especially during high-intensity exercise, while promoting fat oxidation and potentially aiding weight loss in some individuals. It may also cause short-term side effects like headaches and constipation and, if sustained, risks inadequate intake of fiber and certain micronutrients unless carefully planned. Overall, it can be effective for specific goals but requires monitoring for nutritional adequacy and individual tolerance.  
CONFIDENCE: 85
